summary.text: A 31-year-old man with no significant medical history was brought by emergency medical service after one hour of dyspnea. At the scene he had unstable vital signs, including blood pressure 100/65 mm Hg and SpO2 88% on room air. Dyspnea, blood pressure and SpO2 worsened despite saline and oxygen, and he developed generalized urticaria. In the emergency department he had severe respiratory distress, pruritic urticarial lesions, poor vital signs and decreased bronchial sounds in the left lung.

Anaphylactic shock was considered, so oxygen therapy, hydration (intravenous fluids per the abstract) and intramuscular epinephrine were given. A RUSH exam ruled out other causes of shock. Overall three epinephrine doses and 3 liters of normal saline were given for persistent symptoms, with corticosteroids and antihistamines also prescribed. Routine laboratory results were normal. After approximately 4 h of medical care his skin lesions, oxygen levels and blood pressure improved and he stabilized.

Because of severe respiratory distress and abnormal auscultation, portable chest radiography and then a spiral lung CT were done. Imaging showed massive cystic foci measuring 145, 100 and 173 mm, lower lung collapse, detachment of the inner layer close to a pericardial effusion with an air-fluid level and a water lily sign. HRCT findings established anaphylactic shock after rupture of a left lung hydatid cyst; serology was not performed.

After management of the anaphylactic reaction he was transferred to the thoracic surgery center, where a wedge resection of the left lung was performed and a chest tube inserted. Six days after surgery he was discharged in good condition with instructions to take albendazole and schedule follow-up appointments.

article_limitations: Single case report; no tables and no supplements. Figure 1 caption says chest CT but the pixels show a single frontal projection image (modality not settled by the text).
The cystic dimensions, effusion size and air-fluid/water lily findings are not tied in the text to one named imaging study or structure.
Corticosteroid and antihistamine names, doses, routes and times, and the epinephrine dose amounts, are not stated.
Albendazole dose and duration given in the discussion are a recommendation and are not recorded as this patient's prescription.
General statements about hydatid disease, cited cases of other patients and population frequencies in the introduction and discussion are not patient facts.
